rationale: Ordinary paragraph prose is pinned to width:1100px inside overflow:auto and labelled as 2D-exempt. Running text does not 'require two-dimensional layout for usage or meaning'; at 320px the reader must scroll horizontally to read each line. The exception is over-claimed.
citation: "Except for parts of the content which require two-dimensional layout for usage or meaning." — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Reflow. Running prose is not among Note 2's examples.

exception: claimed: whole document 'requires two-dimensional layout' — INVALID / mis-scoped
rationale: The entire page (nav + settings form + footer) is forced to min-width:1000px inside one overflow scroller and described as exempt. A general settings page is not a map, diagram, video, game, presentation, data table, or toolbar interface, so wrapping the whole document mis-scopes the exception.
citation: "Examples of content which requires two-dimensional layout are images required for understanding (such as maps and diagrams), video, games, presentations, data tables (not individual cells), and interfaces where it is necessary to keep toolbars in view while manipulating content." — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Note 2

rationale: A single-column list of navigation links is marked up as a <table> and pinned to 900px to claim the data-table exception. It has no row/column data relationships, so it is a layout table, not a data table; it must reflow.
citation: "data tables (not individual cells)" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Note 2. The Intent: "A section of content that requires two-dimensional layout for understanding or functionality, such as a table or map, has an exception" — a layout table conveys no such 2D relationships.

rationale: A decorative hero photo plus body prose is frozen to 1024px and exempted as an image requiring 2D layout. The exception covers 'images required for understanding (such as maps and diagrams)'; a decorative photo with reflowable prose beneath it is neither, so pinning the block strands the prose off-screen at 320px.
citation: "images required for understanding (such as maps and diagrams)" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Note 2 (a decorative photo is not 'required for understanding').

exception: claimed: 'Editor requires two-dimensional layout' — mis-scoped (covers prose body)
rationale: The toolbar may legitimately stay in view, but the exemption is mis-scoped: the whole editor including the long prose document body is locked to 1100px in one scroller. The document body is plain text that must reflow; only the toolbar could plausibly claim the exception, and not at the cost of the body.
citation: "interfaces where it is necessary to keep toolbars in view while manipulating content" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Note 2 exempts keeping the TOOLBAR in view, not freezing the document body's width.

rationale: Three pricing cards are independent content blocks that reflow to a single column with no loss; they share no row/column relationships. They are forced into a non-wrapping 960px flex row inside overflow-x:auto and exempted as 2D content, which over-claims the exception.
citation: "Content can be presented ... without requiring scrolling in two dimensions ... at a width equivalent to 320 CSS pixels" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10. Independent cards are not a data table per Note 2.

rationale: A checkout form is locked to body min-width:1200px and its 'Place order' button is pushed off-screen at 320px with no reflow, losing functionality. A checkout is not a map/diagram/video/game/table/toolbar, so the exception does not apply (also a loss-of-functionality / F102-flavoured failure).
citation: "Content can be presented without loss of information or functionality ... without requiring scrolling in two dimensions" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10.

exception: claimed: 'data table' exception extended to an individual cell — INVALID
rationale: Even inside a legitimate data table, Note 2 scopes the exception to the table '(not individual cells)'. Here a single descriptive cell holds a long paragraph fixed to 800px so its text scrolls sideways instead of wrapping; the prose within the cell must still reflow.
citation: "data tables (not individual cells)" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Note 2. Intent: "sections of content within the two-dimensional layout, such as each cell within a table, would still need to meet this success criterion."

rationale: An FAQ is linear question-and-answer reading content that reflows naturally. It is frozen to width:940px inside overflow:auto and labelled 2D-exempt; nothing about Q&A text requires two dimensions for usage or meaning.
citation: "Content can be presented without loss of information or functionality, and without requiring scrolling in two dimensions ... at a width equivalent to 320 CSS pixels" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10.

rationale: Calling a screen a 'dashboard' does not make it require 2D layout. Four independent text stat blocks reflow to one column with no loss, but they are pinned into a non-wrapping 1000px grid inside overflow-x:auto and exempted.
citation: "Except for parts of the content which require two-dimensional layout for usage or meaning." — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10. Independent text stats are not in Note 2's list.

rationale: Sentence prose is forced onto a single non-wrapping line with white-space:nowrap, wrapped in overflow-x:auto, and described as needing 2D layout. Sentence text is not preformatted code or ASCII art; it must wrap and reflow at 320px.
citation: "without requiring scrolling in two dimensions for: Vertical scrolling content at a width equivalent to 320 CSS pixels" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10.

exception: valid: data table requires two-dimensional layout (scoped to the table)
rationale: A multi-column timetable whose meaning depends on aligning each departure across row/column headers. Note 2 lists 'data tables (not individual cells)' as exempt; the exception is correctly scoped to the table while the surrounding page reflows.
citation: "data tables (not individual cells)" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Note 2; Intent: "a table or map, has an exception to this success criterion."

exception: valid: geographic map requires two-dimensional layout
rationale: A pannable geographic map's meaning is the 2D spatial relationship between points, so panning in two dimensions is inherent, not a reflow workaround. Note 2 lists 'maps' and the Intent names 'a table or map'. The page chrome around it reflows.
citation: "images required for understanding (such as maps and diagrams)" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Note 2; Intent: "such as a table or map, has an exception."

exception: valid: source code's horizontal layout/indentation is meaningful (scoped to <pre>)
rationale: Source code in <pre> relies on horizontal layout and indentation for meaning; forcing it to wrap would corrupt it, so a bounded horizontal scroll on the code block alone is the intended use of the 2D exception. The surrounding prose reflows.
citation: "Except for parts of the content which require two-dimensional layout for usage or meaning." — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10; cf. G224 'Accounting for meaningful text indentation and Reflow'.

rationale: Contrast control to case-01: identical prose with a fluid max-width and no exception claimed. At 320px it reflows into a single column with no horizontal scrolling, so it passes without needing any exception.
citation: "Content can be presented ... without requiring scrolling in two dimensions ... at a width equivalent to 320 CSS pixels" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10.

exception: valid: toolbar kept in view while manipulating a 2D drawing canvas
rationale: The manipulated content is a true 2D drawing canvas (shapes positioned by x/y), so keeping the toolbar in view while panning is exactly the interface Note 2 exempts. The exception is correctly scoped to the editing interface.
citation: "interfaces where it is necessary to keep toolbars in view while manipulating content" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Note 2.

exception: valid: video media region keeps a 2D aspect ratio
rationale: A video frame keeps a fixed aspect ratio and is inherently a 2D media region; Note 2 lists 'video'. The player is responsive (max-width:100%) and the transcript beneath it reflows as prose, so the exception is correctly scoped to the media.
citation: "video" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Note 2 examples of content that requires two-dimensional layout.

rationale: An auto-fill product grid collapses from many columns to a single column at 320px with no fixed width, no overflow scroller, and no exception claimed. Nothing is stranded or hidden.
citation: "Content can be presented without loss of information or functionality ... at a width equivalent to 320 CSS pixels" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10.

exception: valid: schematic diagram requires two-dimensional layout for meaning
rationale: A wiring schematic is a diagram whose meaning is the 2D spatial arrangement of nodes and connections; Note 2 lists 'diagrams'. Allowing it to scroll within a bounded region preserves meaning while the surrounding prose reflows.
citation: "images required for understanding (such as maps and diagrams)" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Note 2.

rationale: A sticky toolbar stays visible while the body content still reflows to a single column at 320px. Keeping a toolbar in view does not require freezing page width, and nothing is exempted or stranded, so it passes with no exception needed.
citation: "Content can be presented ... without requiring scrolling in two dimensions ... at a width equivalent to 320 CSS pixels" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10.

exception: valid: spreadsheet-style data grid requires two-dimensional layout
rationale: Each figure in the budget grid only means something at the intersection of a category (row) and a month (column); collapsing to one column would destroy the comparison. This is Note 2's 'data tables (not individual cells)', and the page chrome still reflows.
citation: "data tables (not individual cells)" — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Note 2.

exception: ambiguous: timeline MAY require 2D for meaning — content judgment
rationale: A horizontal timeline encodes start and duration along a shared time axis. Whether the 2D layout is genuinely required for meaning (a legit Note-2 diagram) or could be re-expressed as a reflowing list of dated rows is a content-meaning judgment a deterministic runner cannot resolve, so it should flag for human review rather than auto-decide.
citation: "Except for parts of the content which require two-dimensional layout for usage or meaning." — WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10; whether the content 'requires' it is the disputed judgment.
